headline: Single-cell profiling resolves cell states in lung repair, fibrosis, and regeneration
label: Single Cell Profiling Tissue Repair
summary: Recent studies apply single-cell transcriptomics and regulatory network inference to resolve repair-associated cell states in fibrosis and regeneration.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell transcriptomic resolution of cell states during repair and fibrosis, most prominently in the lung. Pulmonary fibrosis niche reviews describe fibroblast crosstalk and microenvironment remodeling after repetitive alveolar micro-injury, and CD63hi macrophages are defined as a terminal inflammatory state in severe COVID-19 lung immunopathology. Fibroblast-to-hematopoietic reprogramming is profiled by single-cell long-read RNA-seq, and polyethylene microplastic exposure is linked to fibroblast reprogramming and immune microenvironment changes in the lung. What is new is the preprint on cytoskeletal-nuclear control of alveolar fibroblast identity, which frames mechanical signals transmitted to the nucleus as regulators of cell fate in lung regeneration. Other items, including a Geneformer-based analysis of hematopoietic stem cell aging, extend single-cell regulatory network approaches beyond repair contexts.
